item.title: Re: Elevator draft, agaiin
item.content:encoded:
It would be good to keep in mind I'm new to the foundation and haven't made an scp yet, so take my criticism with a grain of salt, but these are all the things I noticed while reading it, in the same order as the article.

my (nitpicky) criticism
 my (nitpicky) criticism

I don't get why it would be esoteric? seems like it would be safe, because they can just keep it in one place, no one else has access.

If the O-5 want people to give sightings of Dr. Spencer why would they cover his eyes? I would find a different image if you can't fully show that one.

The forewords are a bit confusing, I didn't immediately know you were talking about the d class, so some disambiguation about that would be good.

Another thing about Test 1 is Dr. Spencer seems oddly unclinical, his words themselves make grammatical sense but it definitely doesn't seem clinical. He should be stating things more factually, instead of words like "hey", "you're welcome", or "lots". It just seems like he should be less replying to the D class, and more telling him what to do in a stricter way.

The diary seems good to me, clinical tone isn't required obviously, but it does seem a bit hamfisted at the end there when he mentions the scp and how he wants to use it all in one sentence at the end.

I thought Test 2 was nice, but it felt a bit forced when you said "Always talked about the 1969 Moon landing". And again, I don't really think a doctor should be saying "hey" during procedure.

The second diary entry seemed better, because it was already established that he wanted to use the elevator, so I don't think a change needs to be present in my opinion.

I like that in the 3rd test, you specify that you're talking about the D-class this time, but I'm not sure why it didn't happen before. The Foreword of this is by far the best of the 3, it doesn't feel especially forced and gives a nice overview of the D class. The test itself seemed fine, but again, Dr. Spencer seems way too non-clinical. Also I don't think there's such a thing as Kauai Beach. Kauai is an Island in Hawaii, but I may be wrong on there being no beach.

Final diary is alright, but I'm confused how he managed to nab 2 pills of scp-500, as those are under super strict lockdown with weight sensors. I also thought the reference to 939 was forced, and there wasn't any mention of him working anywhere near those before.

Overall, the most glaring issues were it being esoteric, the test logs being non-clinical and there were a lot of things that came out of nowhere, like the 939 reference, the moon landing bit, or the sudden diary entry saying he wanted to use the elevator.

Although it might sound like I don't like it, I think this is actually a pretty solid idea, and one that could work really well. As was said in previous thread's criticism, there are other transportation scps, but I can't remember any very similar to this. I would also add a bit more to the description, like if they can interact with the other people there (if any), and if they can, what it looks like to the people in those locations when the elevator comes in (this could be determined by having someone go, finding out their favorite location, sending people to that area, then sending them again).

item.title: JS Staff Post -- Forum Crit -- Info
item.content:encoded:
Author,

Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

 **Seeking Greenlights:** Put yes or no. **Page Type:** SCP Article, Tale, GoI Format, Joke SCP, Site Dossier, Other (specify) **Genre (Optional):** Horror, Drama/Emotional, Comedy, Action, History, Other (specify) **Page Layout (Optional):** [How will you will structure the page in terms of information presentation, or plot development? If you plan on using a unique format/format screw, describe that here.] **Elevator Pitch:** [What is the basic core idea? Use a bullet point list if necessary.] **Central Narrative:** [Describe the story beats or overarching context/"big picture" for your piece. If there is no story content, put "none".] **Hook/Attention-Grabber:** [What is novel/unique about your premise? What is special about your idea here that will make it stand out among the other works already on the mainsite?] **Additional Notes:** [Note any concerns or particular areas of assistance you would like reviewers to focus on.]

Rather than posting a new comment, edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment.

Remember that the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

Once you have revised your post accordingly, please reach out to reviewers to request that they look at your thread. You can find example lists of contacts in the Required Reading thread linked above.

item.title: Re: What award would somebody get for neutralizing a keter?
item.content:encoded:
If someone were to accidentally neutralize a keter, the foundation would be extremely suspicious. Heck, scp 181 just survived a keter twice and they knew something was up. I'm assuming your story is gonna cover that, but just know the research into him would be extensive. As for an award, they would probably give him quite a few leisure privileges, potentially letting him choose his assignment, potentially a pay raise, and likely other things you would expect from exceeding well in a job. Keep in mind that that's all for if the foundation actually wanted the thing dead, if they wanted to experiment with it more, he could potentially even get punished for neutralizing it.

item.title: The chamber of eternity
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Regular SCP page, with Containment Procedures, Descriptions, And addendums

Elevator Pitch: A Chamber is found off the coast of Great Britain covered in strange runes the Foundation can't translate. This chamber allows for short-distance multiversal travel, connecting to around 4 other universes. One person is required to link themselves to this chamber, and then other instances of them can travel through into the present reality. Fondation uses this to connect to other Foundation's, and using their information to collect anomalies before they become an issue.

Central Narrative:

+ Yesyes click on me
- Here you go !!!!!

A junior researcher with a strong background in multiversal studies is selected to link themself to this chamber, by entering inside and connecting them self to other versions of themself. Other foundation instances of this junior researcher come through, and they provide valuable insight into the several SCP's this reality did not possess. The other instances include
1. A site director.
2. a very high ranking officer in the foundation's military division, and is in far better shape then the main junior researcher,
3. Still a junior scientist, but from a universe where the Foundation is on great diplomatic terms with the Wanderer's Library, so this version has various thaumaturgic capabilities.
4. The only one is not a foundation member, but is an avid Parawatch user, and her insight is useful enough to keep around, albeit with the caveat that she will be amentisied before returning to her home plane.
Over time, The main junior researcher reports a decreased emotionally stability, and requests various times to be released from the project, citing "These other versions of me are way smarter and i'm just a burden on studying this project." His requests are not given. All signs point to the main version of this researcher snapping, and then the version that isn't a foundation member is shown trying to take out the one with the thaumaturgy, which obviously doesn't go well. Using the help of the other versions translate's the runes to say "May your strong leaders enter, and the strongest leader exit.”

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The containment procedures will mention how SCP-XXXX-1 goes through several physiological evaluations through out the course of the chamber being active, and different versions of themself are to be kept apart. They will be written to show a lot of precaution for a
Thaumiel object.

Additional Notes: The ancient group that created this object will be present in every alternative reality, but not the main one. This chamber was used by the king’s of this country to prove they were the strongest possible version of themselves.

item.title: Idea Critique: Staff conflicted morals on a anomalous site.
item.content:encoded:
Greenlight Status: Seeking

Page Type: SCP Document (and accompanying tale about prison break after greenlight)

Premise: The premise is about an anomalous village filled with people (SCP-XXXX-1 or -1s) that are generally harmless inside, but if they get out they could be dangerous (how they are dangerous is to be determined, but not world-ending - maybe just dangerous to the civilian populace). The staff are instructed to not sympathize, but are not told what will happen if they do.

Hook: The catch and twist of the story is how the staff fight each other from the ones who want to let the -1s out, and the ones who want to keep them contained. There will probably be a separate tale about both sides of the conflict if this is greenlighted.

Basically about conflicting morals for foundation staff, and who is the "bad guy" - letting the -1s out, or keeping them contained.

item.title: Re: The Goddess Fertility Engine
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for your feedback! I as an author do know what is going on somewhat, but I also like to leave it up for an element of mystery. Lemme give you some answers to the questions posed in the first portion. 1. I’m going to choose to leave it unknown to whether it actually causes these events, but maybe through addendums mention different scenarios where it appeared to let the reader question whether the object itself could cause these events. 2. The object only appears then because that is when it would make sense to “restart” if one of these events devastated the earth. However, it is still useful beyond repopulating a new planet, if the foundation was to procure it its use would be incredibly beneficial. 3. Someone put it there I’m not just going to brush that one aside. But at the same time I think it ruins the fun to give the whole picture, but I will include teases during the draft. The why of course is to start a new human civilization, but their motives behind it are unclear.
4. It isn’t a goddess but it has all the prowess of one, hence its abilities that make it equivalent to what we can perceive as the potential of god. Like what a god could do that is perceivable to humans.
Now for your second question list

SCP-507 discovered it and then subsequently saw 20 over a long span of time, which the foundation had requested him to document. The foundation knows it only appears then due to one instance where 507 observed the transformation process of the woman inside the SCP into a “goddess” at which point the machine began to play a message that despite being in an unfamiliar gibberish, 507 was able to comprehend. The message details why the machine is there and leaves a message for the remaining residents of the planet. Plus the landscape around each area where an instance of the scp had been found was decimated or entirely void of life, or it was apparent that humanity had been replaced by a different species in the dominance hierarchy.

It seemed you were unclear about this but the foundation doesn’t have this machine contained, which means they can only run tests that 507 can conduct on his own. you also missed that I said the woman would grow in size, and then the machine would leave orbit, because removal of the woman is impossible. Anyway, please tell me if this has helped clear up questions! And if you have rebuttles please let me know

item.title: Re: The Goddess Fertility Engine
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello! Not an official critter here, but I can read and share my thoughts.
And my thoughts here are that there isn't enough to make a call.
Sure, the Foundation may not know exactly what's going on. That's sort of the main point, they're making the best of a situation that goes beyond human understanding. But you as the author usually want to have a very good idea of what is happening.

I'm not telling you to figure out every little detail, of course. "It's anomalous" is still a valid argument. But I think that leaving almost all of it open-ended (does it cause K-class events or not? Why does it only appear then? Who put it there? Why? Is it really a goddess? And so on) makes it look like it's you who doesn't have a good idea of how your story will work. I'm not saying you don't! I'm sure you do have a very good plan for how it all fits together in mind. You just need to write it down better, I feel.

Which leads me to point #2: What's the story you're trying to tell? SCPs nowadays to be succesful 'need' a story, from what I understand. At least, it is very much recommended to have one. A narrative beyond 'here is an object, and it does X. The foundation is investigating it'.
For example, the first ideas that come to my mind at least are questions like "what happens to the woman once she's removed?", "How was this machine found?", and "How many K-Class events have happened such that they know it only appears then? Conversely, do they monitor this machine so that they know when a K-Class event is starting? Do they have someone in standby there at all times? Is it ethical for them to basically have a woman assigned to this role?"

Again, these are all just off the top of my head. There are probably a thousand other ways this idea could be developed, but I hope I gave you some prompts to help you do so!

Forum thread: The Goddess Fertility Engine

item.title: Licensing Staff Post
item.content:encoded:
On the EN wiki, we allow it on the basis that EN plans to forward port from BY-SA 3.0 to BY-SA 4.0 on an unspecified date in the future.

Other wikis may have a more strict view of the licensing policy. In that case, you would want to check with them to see what their specific rules are when dealing with 4.0 images should you plan on posting there.

Be advised if your article survives and gets translated, wikis that prohibit 4.0 images will not be including the image with the translation.


Forum category: Per Page Discussions / Per page discussions
Forum thread: Image Use Policy

Your canon cannot be "finished."

Does this mean that a canon cannot be a story that can at some point be concluded (i.e. a canon should be a setting, rather than a storyline), or just that the storyline cannot be concluded as of the time of posting (i.e. a canon can be considered "complete" at some point, just not at the time of posting)?

If it's the former, then there are a few canons that should probably get relabeled, as the entire point of them is to advance a single main storyline, with any non-main storyline entries being relegated to at best auxiliary status (off the top of my head, Rezz, Competitive Eschatology [love you, moose <3]).

If it's the latter, and closed or completed storyline-based canons are taken off the page, then that seems like a defacto ban on storyline-based canons, just with extra steps ("This can be on the page, but once it's completed, then you have to take it off").

If it's the latter and we keep a canon with a completed storyline on the canon page, then what's the point of having the rule about finished canons (or closed canons, for that matter) in the first place?

I'm not advocating for one position or another, but I do think that there is a need for clarity. Part of the issue, imo, was putting the technical cart before the narrative horse. We know exactly how many articles are needed for a canon, but so far as I can tell, there is no clear distinction between a canon and a qualifying series beyond "one's a canon and the other isn't," or even what a canon is/should be.

item.title: Re: The Maw
item.content:encoded:
Oh my… I just typed out a massive, comprehensive response, but wikidot said, "Would be a shame if something happened to it." Here's the cliff notes version:

Location: The temperature (cold=entity grow big fast, hot=entity grow big slower) is a main factor - cold helps smaller entities grow quickly, and solar/thermal energy sustains large entities. The coordinates are just random, but added for authenticity. The portal, admittedly, is more for narrative purposes than anything else - I'll tie it in somehow.

Neutralization: The core of the biomass (the maw and star) is essentially an organic Dyson Sphere. At times, though, it draws hydrogen aggressively from the star, but always at a sustainable rate. The final MTF squad discover something terrible enough that it convinces them to destroy the system with extreme prejudice. In a stroke of genius, one of the members destroys a section of a cortex just below the Maw that controls inhibitions, thus causing the Maw to begin extracting huge quantities of hydrogen. This sends the star into an implosion, and however durable the biomass may be, it cannot survive a dying star. That also destroys the pair of portals—the damage inflicted to the one within the system corresponds to the one on earth.

I know that there's still a bunch of refining to do, and rest assured, I intend to do it. Thanks again for your response!
